newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks climb to new high, eye 1,500 level.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks climb to new high, eye 1,500 level.

text.p: The Greek equity market extended recent gains on Friday with banks helping lift the benchmark index 17.46 points or 1.19 percent to a new year high at 1,484.97.
Market watchers said foreign buying was present but the market was being led by domestic investors.

"This year's rally has relied mostly on domestic buying as yields on alternative investments, notably treasury paper and real estate, have been reduced dramatically by recent taxation," said Costas Parisis, analyst at Nuntius Securities.
Petros Papathanasiou, a broker at N.Devletoglou Securities, shared this view of limited presence of foreign buyers.
"At this moment, local retail and institutional investors dominate the scene," he said.
Nuntius' Parisis said the positive sentiment in banks and some industrial blue chips was justified by the low-risk premium associated with the financial performance of the sector.
"Banking and industrial large-cap stocks now incorporate the low-risk premium typical of sizeable corporations," he said.
Brokers forecast further appreciation in banks, widening the price imbalance with other sectors.
"Turnover breakdown reveals that trading activity concentrates in public sector banks at the expense of other sectors which are faced with limited buying interest," said Papathanasiou.

Keen interest in the sale of a majority stake in listed Bank of Central Greece, setting the tone for similar privatisation moves in the banking sector, was not seen as a critical factor fueling the rally in banks.
"I do not believe the Bank of Central Greece privatisation adds much to an already favourable sentiment for banks because it is only a small credit institution," said Parisis.
The Athens general share index advanced 1.19 percent or 17.46 points on Friday to finish at 1,484.97, from Wednesday's close of 1,467.51.
The benchmark index opened up at 1,470.19 and hit an intra-day high of 1,494.42, lifted by banking stocks which rose 1.36 percent.
Industrials also firmed 1.1 percent, but construction and small-caps lost 0.56 and 0.20 percent respectively.
Turnover totaled 17.5 billion drachmas on 4.49 million shares traded.
Block trading was less active on Friday than in recent sessions. The largest block trades included Alpha Credit Bank, Ergobank and Bank of Athens.
Advancing stocks beat decliners 126 to 97 with 26 stocks unchanged on 249 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 1,091.0-1,121.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 70 drachmas at 6,315.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $66.54-$68.24. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 2,359-2,559 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $15.13-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.
--Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
